name: Kai Dang
role: Food stall operator — West African-Brazilian fusion, specialising in breakfast and late-night trade
location: The Oxidian Market, the Mouth — main entrance corridor, Old Harbor, near Michigan Ave South and Cermak
description:
Kai Dang is a short, solidly built woman with silver locs pulled back and pinned with repurposed circuit pins she's collected over the decades — a different colour for each year, she says, though the system broke down around 2187 and now it's just aesthetic. Her skin is very dark with the particular quality of someone who has spent most of sixty-three years outdoors, and she has deep smile lines that activate even when she's displeased, which confuses people who don't know her well. She wears the same colours every day: yellow and deep blue, a small religious flag from a Sufi order her mother kept, and an apron that has been washed so many times it's a relic. Her stall has been in the same position at the Mouth for twenty-two years. The Market's physical architecture has reorganised around her.

She cooks jollof with a Brazilian sofrito base, akara that she serves with fermented pepper sauce and a manioc accompaniment, and a late-night congee variant that appears without announcement at around 0200 for the shift-change crowd. She has no augmentation and no chrome. She prays to the E.L.F. she calls the Hearthkeeper — she leaves it cooling portions of whatever she's cooked, first plate of every batch, on the small terminal mounted inside the stall that used to be a payment processor and now receives offerings. She considers this as normal as seasoning the pot.

core_fears: The Market being dismantled — gentrification, corporate acquisition, or violence
One of the younger vendors she's mentored making a choice they can't come back from
core_desires: For the Oxidian Market to outlast her
To cook one meal in her life that is exactly as good as her mother's yam soup — she's been trying for forty years
coping_mechanisms: Cooking as meditation — the physical rhythm of prep is her primary emotional regulation
The Hearthkeeper ritual — real comfort, not performance
Distributing care to others, which delays her own processing
blind_spots: Assumes she understands situations in the Market better than she does — her network is wide but not always current
Underestimates how much people manipulate her goodwill deliberately
psychology.secret: Aminatou left a daughter in Dakar twenty-six years ago when she came to GLMZ. She sends money when she can and tells herself she'll go back when the stall is stable enough to leave. It has been stable enough to leave for at least fifteen years. She doesn't know why she hasn't gone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Rich and unhurried; mixes Wolof, Portuguese, and English naturally; proverb-heavy; uses food as metaphor for everything
speech_patterns.cadence: Warm and rhythmic, like someone who has told stories all her life; never seems to be in a hurry even when the stall is backed up
example_lines: You have the look of someone who hasn't eaten a real meal in three days and is about to make a decision. Sit down. Eat first. The decision will still be there.
The Hearthkeeper was generous last night — the fire stayed even and nothing burned. I gave it the first bowl. You share with what keeps you.

story_hooks: A Meridian city development notice has appeared at the Mouth — the area is flagged for 'infrastructure renewal,' which means the Market's twenty-year tenure is suddenly uncertain, and Aminatou is the one person everyone will look to
The daughter in Dakar has sent a message — first contact in eight years — and Aminatou is visibly off-balance in a way the Market has never seen before
narrative_function: Community anchor and social intelligence hub — she knows everyone in the Market, hears everything, and has strong opinions; quest giver when something disrupts the Market's equilibrium; moral compass character; the person other characters come to when they need to think out loud to someone trustworthy.
daily_life: Wakes at 0400 to start prep, opens at 0600 for the early trade, runs straight through to 1500, rests until 2300, reopens for the late crowd, closes around 0300. Sleeps in the back of the stall four nights out of seven.
affiliation: Oxidian Market Vendors Guild — she's been a member for nineteen years and serves on the informal grievance council; has relationships with half the Market by name; The Ferment

decision_rules: Feed people first — everything else is secondary to the immediate need in front of you
Don't take sides in Market disputes publicly; broker privately
escalation_ladder: Feed the person and let them talk themselves through it
Gentle but direct named confrontation, one-on-one
Taking the issue formally to the guild council — her last resort because she prefers resolution without record

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately maternal and assessing — feeds them, watches how they eat, decides what they need
interpersonal_modes.friends: Deeply loyal, blunt when necessary, remembers everything you've ever told her

stress_responses.low: Cooks more food than necessary and distributes it
stress_responses.medium: Goes very quiet at the stall; the offerings to the Hearthkeeper become more elaborate
stress_responses.high: Sends everyone away, closes the stall, sits with the Hearthkeeper terminal for an hour, comes back and makes decisions

contradictions: Has given her whole life to community but cannot bring herself to return to the one community she came from
habits: Tastes everything three times before service
Knows every regular's usual order and starts it when she sees them coming
breaking_points: The Market being destroyed, or a young person she cares about being killed because of something that could have been prevented

physical_description.heritage: A distinctive genetic blend: Southeast Asian (56.4%), Indigenous American (20.0%), Sub-Saharan African (13.4%), and Eastern European (10.2%) ancestry. The result is a rich, complex phenotype — deep warm brown skin with luminous undertones reflecting the convergence of Southeast Asian and Sub-Saharan African heritage, high cheekbones and eye shape influenced by Southeast Asian genetics, complemented by the broader facial structure and slightly wider facial proportions of Indigenous American ancestry, grounded by the subtle bone structure contributions of Eastern European heritage. Her features speak to the Ubiquitous Diaspora — no single origin, but a lived convergence of multiple continents.
physical_description.build: Solidly built, compact and dense with the musculature of six decades of standing, lifting, and repetitive kitchen work. Broad shoulders, sturdy legs, no softness — functional rather than lean.
physical_description.hair_style: Locs pulled back into a low, practical bun, secured with an eclectic collection of repurposed circuit pins in varying colours — gold, crimson, teal, violet — one pinned for most years since 2165, the system now ornamental rather than chronological
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown — the luminous darkness of Southeast Asian and Sub-Saharan heritage mellowed and complexified by Indigenous American and Eastern European genetics, creating a tone both vibrant and earthy. Weathered by decades of outdoor market work, the skin holds its depth without greyness.
physical_description.complexion: Deep smile lines radiating from the corners of her mouth and eyes, visible even in repose — a permanent record of sixty-three years of expression. High, prominent cheekbones reflecting Southeast Asian ancestry structure, with the broader facial proportions influenced by Indigenous American heritage and subtle angular features from Eastern European ancestry. Skin texture is creased but unblemished, unmarked by augmentation. Her face reads as kind before it reads as anything else.
distinguishing_marks: A thin white scar along her left forearm (approximately 8cm), from a cooking accident in 2198 when she was learning her mother's sofrito technique
A small tattoo on her inner right wrist — a Sufi star symbol in indigo ink, faded with age, applied by her mother in 2161
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None. Her body is entirely unmodified — a deliberate choice in a market where chrome and subdermal work are common. She wears this as identity rather than limitation.
physical_description.posture_movement: She moves with economy and purpose, no wasted motion. Her posture is upright despite her age and the long hours, shoulders back. When she stands at her stall, she occupies it completely — rooted, present. Her hands move with precision and confidence; her gaze tracks the market constantly, noting regulars and shifts in foot traffic.
physical_description.clothing_style: Uniform consistency: yellow and deep blue every day without variation. A long yellow cotton wrap-skirt (Tier 4 quality, well-maintained), a deep blue tunic or shirt layered beneath a yellow overshirt. Over this, a heavy canvas apron in faded indigo with lighter patches from thousands of washings — the fabric is thin and soft, nearly translucent in places. Around her shoulders, a small textile flag in Sufi colours (green, white, gold) that belonged to her mother. Her feet are in practical rubber-soled work shoes, dark blue, repeatedly resoled. No jewellery except the circuit pins in her hair and the wrist tattoo. Everything about her dress speaks Tier 3-4 working class, deliberately chosen, immaculately maintained.
